title: From Demo to Production- Building Enterprise AI Agents That Actually Work with Microsoft Copilot Studio with Elliot Margot [MVP]
description:
Many AI agents look impressive in a demo but fail in production because of governance gaps, poor data and runaway costs. This episode helps Copilot Studio makers, architects and IT leaders move from chatbot experiments to secure, governed enterprise agents with RAG, MCP and multi-agent designs.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro and Elliot's journey into generative AI06:56 – Why enterprise AI is hard: governance and DLP10:43 – Selling AI to executive sponsors: ROI and the wow effect16:17 – Multi-agent systems and orchestration21:06 – RAG, metadata, versioning and chunking27:38 – MCP explained31:05 – Governance, DLP and citizen development47:46 – The future of agents, model choice and token costs
Key takeaways
Enterprises learn AI governance fastest by building small solutions while steadily improving DLP policies, sensitivity labels and monitoring rather than waiting for a perfect model.Good RAG depends on good data: well-described metadata, a clean production knowledge base without outdated versions, and careful chunking keep answers accurate and token costs down.Production agents need clearly communicated tasks, tightly scoped connectors, manual testing and the right model size, because small language models are often enough and endless agent loops can become expensive.
Worth quoting
“You can't see the results of the governance in place if you don't start. So you can have to start while building it.” – Elliot Margot (08:48)
“Maybe you want to remove a MailChimp, if it's not in your scope, really keep the scope small, so that you're not able to use things that you shouldn't be able to.” – Elliot Margot (33:05)
